title: Article 100 — Voting in Houses, power of Houses to act notwithstanding vacancies, and quorum

content.overview: Article 100 provides that, save as otherwise provided in the Constitution, questions in either House or joint sitting are decided by a majority of votes of members present and voting (Chairman/Speaker has a casting vote in case of equality). Either House may act notwithstanding vacancies. Until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the quorum is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House. If there is no quorum, the Chairman/Speaker must adjourn or suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.
content.glance: Majority of present and voting; casting vote of Chair; House may act despite vacancies; quorum = 1/10 until Parliament provides otherwise.
content.study:
Article 100:

(1) Save as otherwise provided in this Constitution, all questions at any sitting of either House or joint sitting of the Houses shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or person acting as Chairman or Speaker. The Chairman or Speaker, or person acting as such, shall not vote in the first instance but shall have and exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

(2) Either House of Parliament shall have power to act notwithstanding any vacancy in the membership thereof, and any proceedings in Parliament shall be valid notwithstanding that it is discovered subsequently that some person who was not entitled so to do sat or voted or otherwise took part in the proceedings.

(3) Until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament shall be one-tenth of the total number of members of the House.

(4) If at any time during a meeting of a House there is no quorum, it shall be the duty of the Chairman or Speaker, or person acting as such, either to adjourn the House or to suspend the meeting until there is a quorum.

Examination: majority of present and voting; casting vote; validity despite vacancies/unqualified participation; quorum 1/10; duty to adjourn/suspend if no quorum.

sections.heading: Voting
sections.body: Majority of members present and voting (unless Constitution provides otherwise). Chair does not vote in the first instance; casting vote on equality.

sections.heading: Vacancies and quorum
sections.body: House may act notwithstanding vacancies; proceedings valid despite later discovery of unqualified participation. Quorum: one-tenth of total membership (until Parliament by law provides otherwise). No quorum → adjourn or suspend.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain voting and quorum under Article 100.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 100, questions are decided by a majority of votes of members present and voting; the Chairman/Speaker has a casting vote on equality and does not vote in the first instance. Either House may act notwithstanding vacancies, and proceedings remain valid despite later discovery that an unqualified person took part. Quorum is one-tenth of the total membership of the House until Parliament by law provides otherwise; without quorum the Chair must adjourn or suspend the meeting.
